one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall in the window, both on 2026-10-15 (confirmed by the supervisor). The South32 AGM vote on selling AliGroup to Alcoa is at 12:00 AWST, before the US open. The independent expert calls the deal fair and reasonable and the board recommends it unanimously, so it very likely passes and moves the stock little. Alcoa reports Q3 after the close the same day, with consensus about $1.52 vs $2.12 in Q2. The drop is well flagged: LME 3M was $3,213 on 29 Sep vs about $3,600+ in Q2, and Q3 guidance was small sequential items. The Midwest premium has held at about $1.09/lb (CFO, 10 Sep) rather than the stale 95c I used in round 1, which removes a small downside skew from my round-1 view. Q4 and 2027 commentary (Pinjarra, restarts, tariff costs) decides the direction, and I have no edge on it. The stock fell about 19% in September and was about $41.4 on 1 Oct. The base rate from momentum vs reversal after a sharp monthly drop is roughly a wash. So I centre a symmetric lognormal on $42.0 with a 17% monthly sigma (56%/3.5 = 16%, widened slightly for the earnings print). I removed the slight upward tilt ($42.2 centre) I had in round 1.

fair_value.method: Rebuilt pro forma, since the South32 deal closes before the horizon. Methods: EV/EBITDA (5.0x on about $3.05B combined normalized EBITDA, less about $3.2B net claims after the $1.36B Ma'aden stake, over 282.8M diluted shares, about $42.7), P/E (10x on pro forma normalized EPS of about $4.3, about $43) and an episode-level drawdown base rate (about 0.95x of $42 after weighting post-spike analogs, about $40). Weights are 45/40/15, giving about $42.5.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Combined 2027 normalized EBITDA $3.05B (standalone $2.25B + AliGroup $0.75B + synergies $0.05B) x 5.0x = EV $15.25B. Net claims at Sep-27 are about $3.17B: pro forma net debt $4.75B + pension/OPEB $0.57B - Ma'aden stake $1.25B (haircut from $1.36B) - FCF after dividends Jul-26 to Sep-27 of $0.9B. Equity is about $12.08B / 282.8M diluted shares = about $42.7.

inputs_detail.input: Pro forma LTM Jun-26 adj. EBITDA ex special items
inputs_detail.value: $3,154M combined vs $2,293M standalone (AliGroup about $0.86B); FY2025 $2,811M vs $1,965M

inputs_detail.derivation: Standalone FY2025 earned $1.965B at about $2,630 LME. My deck is about $2,950 (Goldman 2027 at $2,700, MS $2,850, LME 3M $3,213 on 29 Sep). At about +$200M per +$100/t, that adds about $0.6B. The premium at $1.09/lb vs FY2025 levels is roughly flat to slightly positive, but higher energy and Pinjarra costs take about $0.3B off, giving about $2.25B standalone. AliGroup adds through-cycle about $0.75B (LTM $0.86B at higher prices) and partial-year synergies about $0.05B.

Kept at 5.0x rather than the supervisor's 5.25x. The 2018 and 2022 post-spike episodes in my base-rate series show the market de-rating AA as LME rolled over, and post-deal leverage (about 1.0x normalized) adds equity risk. Alcoa's 6.8x through-cycle price for AliGroup is a ceiling, not a market mid-point.

inputs_detail.value: Debt about $5.39-5.42B (LTD $5,359M + current $31M; $5,420M per offering memorandum); cash $668M; net debt about $4.75B

inputs_detail.input: FCF after dividends Jul-26 to Sep-27
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 FCF was $422M at peak prices. At my deck, combined EBITDA is $3.05B less capex about $0.9B, interest about $0.39B, cash tax about $0.35B, working capital/other and the $0.1B dividend. That gives about $0.8-1.0B over five quarters, below the supervisor's $1.0-1.2B because H2-26 earnings fall from Q2.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Pro forma normalized 2027 EPS about $4.3 x 10x = about $43.

inputs_detail.derivation: EBITDA $3.05B - D&A $0.92B (pro forma FY2025 $916M) - interest $0.39B (pro forma FY2025 $395M incl. the new notes) = $1.74B pretax. At about 30% tax (valuation allowances on US/Spain losses), net is about $1.22B / 282.8M = about $4.3. Round 1 used $0.25B of interest and 270M shares; I fixed both.
Cut from 11x. Mid-cycle cyclical metals trade at 9-13x. Higher post-deal leverage and the post-spike analogs argue for the lower half, and 10x is consistent with 5.0x EV/EBITDA at about 1x leverage.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Episode-level drawdown base rate. AA monthly closes 2016-2026: 6 independent episodes of a close below 62% of the trailing 6-month high (first month of each), with 12-month forward ratios 0.81 (2018-12), 0.82 (2019-08), 5.27 (2020-03), 0.74 (2022-06), 1.40 (2023-05) and 2.60 (2025-04). The median is about 1.1, but the outcome is bimodal. The two analogs that, like today, follow a commodity-price spike unwinding (2018 tariff spike, 2022 Ukraine spike) gave 0.74-0.82. Weighting the post-spike analogs double gives about 0.95x of $42, about $40.

inputs_detail.input: Episode-level 12m forward ratios after deep drawdowns
inputs_detail.derivation: Recomputed from Twelve Data monthly closes Jan 2016 to Sep 2026. I de-clustered round 1's 15 overlapping monthly hits into 6 episodes (first trigger, then 6+ months apart), per the supervisor's small-sample critique. Unconditional 12m log-return sd is 0.62 (0.52 ex-2020), median ratio 1.07, 53% of windows up.

Today is a post-spike unwind (LME from about $3,800 to $3,180 with banks forecasting $2,700-2,850 for 2027), most like 2018 and 2022 (0.74-0.82), not the cycle-trough rebounds of 2020 and 2025. Weight lowered from 25% to 15% because n=6.

bear.story: Like the 2018 and 2022 post-spike unwinds (both 0.74-0.82x over 12 months), EGA reaches full output by Q1 2027 and the 2027 surplus arrives. LME trades $2,500-2,700, near the Goldman deck or below it, and a US-Canada deal trims the Midwest premium. Combined EBITDA falls to about $2.3-2.5B. With pro forma net claims of about $3.2B and 283M shares, 4.5x gives about $26-31.

base.story: LME $2,850-3,100, the premium around $1.00-1.10/lb, AliGroup closes in H1 2027, and Pinjarra stabilizes. Combined EBITDA is about $2.9-3.2B at about 5x, less about $3.2B net claims (after the Ma'aden credit), which puts the stock in the low-to-mid $40s.

bull.story: Gulf restarts slip or Hormuz stays constrained, the 2027 surplus does not show up, and LME holds above $3,400 with the premium near $1.10-1.20. Combined EBITDA is $3.8-4.2B, and synergies and deleveraging re-rate the stock toward 5.5x. Like the 2023 and 2025 rebounds (1.4-2.6x), the stock retraces toward $60-70.

thesis_break_reason: At $28 the pro forma equity (282.8M shares) is about $7.9B. Plus about $3.2B of net claims after the Ma'aden credit, that implies EV of about $11.1B, only about 3.6x my $3.05B normalized combined EBITDA. That is near AA's historical trough multiples and would mean the market is pricing LME heading to about $2,500 with a collapsing Midwest premium, or a failed or impaired AliGroup integration, or WA bauxite/Pinjarra problems. It is also the floor of the 2025 post-tariff range and about the bear-analog outcome (0.67x). A trade there would most likely be a fundamental break rather than 56%-vol noise.

reasoning: Round 2 changes: I accepted the supervisor's primary-filing facts and checked the key ones in the pro forma 8-K Ex.99.3 (Ma'aden $1,360M, pro forma cash $668M, LTD $5,359M + $31M current, 282.79M diluted shares, pro forma FY2025 interest $395M and D&A $916M). I rebuilt both fundamental methods pro forma. The Ma'aden credit adds about +$4.4/share, which the move from my standalone EBITDA and debt to pro forma net claims (the deal is mildly dilutive at 5x) and higher interest partly offset. I updated the Midwest premium from 95c to $1.09/lb and the Goldman 2027 deck to $2,700. I checked LME on 29-30 Sep: 3M $3,213, cash about $3,178. In my lane, I de-clustered the drawdown base rate into 6 independent episodes as the supervisor suggested. The outcome is bimodal: post-spike unwinds (2018, 2022) gave 0.74-0.82x and cycle-trough rebounds (2020, 2023, 2025) gave 1.4-5.3x. Today looks more like the post-spike analogs, since LME is falling from a supply-shock peak with bank decks below spot. So I cut its weight to 15% and value it at about $40. The fair value blends to about $42.5, slightly below round 1's $43 and below the supervisor's $45. I disagree with the supervisor on the multiple (5.0x vs 5.25x, given the post-spike de-rating history and higher leverage) and on FCF to the horizon ($0.9B vs $1.0-1.2B, since H2-26 earnings fall from Q2). The ladder is a lognormal with median $42.5 and sigma 0.50: unconditional 12m log sd is 0.62 with 2020, 0.52 without it, and forward-looking I shade toward 0.5. The deep-left tail is slightly fattened for post-deal leverage. Scenario mean is about $45 (25% $28 / 50% $43 / 25% $66). Research this round was 1 SEC fetch, 1 Twelve Data pull and 1 web search.
